title: Plan of Care Certification, Recertification and Payer Authorization — Outpatient and Part B Therapy Services
content:
**Outpatient and Part B Therapy Services** — clinical policy on evaluation, certification and authorization of plans of care.

## Policy clauses

> Treatment starts only after an evaluation and a plan of care signed by the physician or practitioner within the initial certification days after the evaluation. A plan runs at most the plan certification maximum before it must be recertified. Medicare Advantage visits need the plan's authorization, with more visits requested when the authorized visits remaining fall to the reauthorization lead; Medical Assistance visits need prior authorization. Therapy to maintain function is covered when skilled care is needed, even without expected improvement. An evaluation that finds no skilled need ends the referral as not indicated.

In every tier the initial certification days are 30 days after the evaluation and the plan certification maximum is 90 days. The reauthorization lead of the Medicare Advantage Outpatient Therapy Plan of Care is 2 authorized visits remaining; the figure is 0 in every other tier, where it does not apply. An evaluation is required before treatment starts in every tier, and a significant change in condition requires a re-evaluation.

## Outcomes of the evaluation

| Evaluation finding | Plan status afterwards | What the record shows |
|---|---|---|
| Skilled therapy is needed; the physician or practitioner signs the plan of care and treatment starts | Active | The evaluation date, the date the plan was signed, the last day the signed plan covers, the visits the payer authorized where authorization applies, and the Medicare Advantage copay per visit from the plan's authorization |
| No need for skilled therapy | Not indicated | The evaluation date and the closing date |

A referral moves from referred to active only on the signed plan after the evaluation, and from referred to not indicated only on an evaluation that finds no skilled need.

## Recertification

A plan runs at most 90 days before it must be recertified. A recertification, or an extension of the payer's authorization, records the recertification date, the new last covered day, the updated authorized visits and the updated copay.

## Payer authorization by tier

| Tier | Authorization the visits need |
|---|---|
| Medicare Advantage Outpatient Therapy Plan of Care | The Medicare Advantage plan's authorization; more visits are requested from the plan when the authorized visits remaining fall to 2 |
| Medical Assistance Therapy Plan of Care | Medical Assistance prior authorization |
| Medicare Part B Physical Therapy, Occupational Therapy and Speech-Language Pathology Plans of Care; Private Pay Therapy Plan of Care | No payer authorization requirement |

## Maintenance therapy

Therapy to maintain function is covered when skilled care is needed, even without expected improvement.

## Illustrations (hypothetical plans)

- Evaluation on 11 September; plan signed on 2 October, 21 days later: within the 30 days, and treatment may start on the signed plan.
- Evaluation on 11 September; plan signed on 24 October, 43 days later: the plan was not signed within the 30 days.
- A Medicare Advantage plan authorized 9 visits and 7 have been furnished: 2 authorized visits remain, so more visits are requested from the plan.
- A resident whose condition is not expected to improve but who needs skilled therapy to maintain function: the therapy is covered.
